messages:
Maya Chen: Heads-up: we're seeing a small but consistent spike in OOMs on prod-gpu-2 after the kernel-selector change last night. Not huge TPS hit but a handful of failed requests every ~5m. :eyes:
Aj Patel: Seen it too. Logs show allocation failure coming from logits slab during finalization step (seq_len ~ 768 workloads).
Leo Rivera: Do we have a repro trace / perf profile? Could be reuse ordering with the new kernel path.
Maya Chen: I ran a quick trace with nvprof and our internal alloc tracer. Attaching excerpt: 
```
AllocTrace: slab_alloc logits 24MB ctx=slot-27
KV cache warm: reserve 48MB
Kernel select -> fused-attn-v2 path
free(logits) deferred until batch finalize
AllocError: out of memory trying to allocate 12MB
```
Aj Patel: That snippet suggests logits buffer eviction happens after KV reserve, so transient high watermark > GPU mem. Kernel change might be increasing kernel workspace a bit which pushes us over.
Sarah K.: I pushed a canary that disables the eager kernel workspace growth heuristic. Will leave it running on canary-2 for an hour.
Leo Rivera: Two ideas: 1) prioritize logits free before KV reserve when finalizing a request (reorder handoff) 2) introduce a soft workspace cap per-request that triggers early logits recycling. Both are small patches.
Maya Chen: Prioritizing free sounds low-risk. But we need to be careful with concurrent reuse: some pools expect ownership until compute fence completes.
Aj Patel: Right. We can add an ownership relay: if fence not ready, mark logits as "reclaimable" and let eviction thread push them to an emergency slab that uses eager-free semantics.
Sarah K.: Can you sketch the change? I can implement the reclaimable flag + emergency slab worker.
Leo Rivera: Something like: 
```
// pseudo:
if (compute_fence.signaled()) { free(buf); } else { buf->mark_reclaimable(); enqueue(emergency_worker, buf); }
// emergency_worker does an eager free after waiting small grace (5ms)
```
Maya Chen: Also add a metric: pool.reclaims.emergency and pool.temp_high_watermark so we can correlate.
Aj Patel: Agreed. Meanwhile, to mitigate, I've patched runtime to cap kernel workspace growth to +10% instead of +35% on that path. Canary looks stable so far (0 OOMs in 15m).
Sarah K.: FYI infra-bot reports a single canary deploy: deploy/canary-2026-03-18 by Sarah K. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: deploy/canary-2026-03-18 succeeded on canary-2 (sha: d4f7b2)
Leo Rivera: If we land the reclaimable/emergency worker approach we should also update the allocator docs: describe semantics and guarantees for reclaimable buffers (best-effort reclaim, not safe for long-lived external pointers).
Maya Chen: Good call. Post-merge checklist: add unit test simulating fence-delayed logits, add perf test to ensure no extra latency >1ms p50, and roll canary to 10% traffic.
Aj Patel: I'll draft the PR with tests. Assigning to @Sarah K. for canary rollout once merged.
Sarah K.: On it. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Maya Chen: Thanks — big win if this removes the OOM spikes. We'll monitor metrics (oom.count, pool.temp_high_watermark) for 6h.
Leo Rivera: Also let's record the profiling artifacts to the perf bucket under runtimes/2026-03-18/logits-reclaim/ so we can replay.
Maya Chen: Logged. Closing loop after 6h. :spiral_calendar:
